old: Start smaller:
new: Can you try a bit smaller?

old: “Show me one body sensation.” “Show me one word.” “Show me whether today is for listening or resting.”
new: Even just to one sensation in your body? Or just one word? Or even if you're going to be listening or resting today?

old: First ask what feels fake: the wording, the image, the expectation, or the role you’re trying to perform. Not experiencing an inner voice or image isn’t, by itself, resistance or a missing adult capacity. Correct an explicitly unwanted invitation. If you recognize a protective part, you can talk to it:
new: Do you know what exactly feels fake? The words, an image, what you are expecting, the role? Just to let you know that it not having an inner voice/image doing this isn't a lack of some grown up-ness or a resistance. If it feels like you're being asked to do something that you don't want to do then correct this. If it feels like a part may be protecting you from doing this then talk to this.

old: “What are you protecting me from?” “Are you afraid I will lie to myself again?” “Are you afraid this is performance?”
new: 'What are you protecting me from?' or 'Are you afraid that I'll lie to myself again?' or 'Are you afraid that it will be performative?'

old: The voice may be the inherited parent enforcing an old belonging rule. Don’t argue with it. Ask which rule it is enforcing and what ordinary evidence would make the new adult voice more believable.
new: It may also be that this is coming from an inner voice of a parent that is forcing a rule onto you to make you feel like you belong. If this is the case then don't argue, find out what the rule is and then work on building evidence for your new adult voice.

old: The fake feeling can also mean that a needed adult capacity isn’t available yet. Stop demanding a convincing voice. If you can already observe what is happening, borrow the particular warmth, boundary, or direction you lack. A real or imagined caring figure can help. Try one believable sentence or action and see how it is received.
new: If it's the feeling of fakeness that is telling you that you don't have some grown up ability then don't try and believe an inner voice for this. As long as you have some observing ego then borrow what you need from someone that you can imagine that has enough (this can be a family member, friend, famous person etc). Try something that rings a bit more true (this can be a sentence, action etc) and see how it goes.

old: Intensity then gets mistaken for meaning. Sometimes the inner child is finally speaking. Sometimes a Protector is showing fear, or shame, grief, anger, longing, and other buried material are asking for care. But an intense state can also be bodily overload, environmental chaos, sleep deprivation, or plain confusion. A frightening image isn’t automatically truth, a bad feeling isn’t automatically a lesson, and a “download” doesn’t deserve belief merely because it came with excellent lighting.
new: One of the problems is that you THINK that because you are in an altered state, that it MEANS something. Sometimes it is your inner child talking, but sometimes it is a Protector showing you their fear, sometimes it is your shame, or grief, or anger, or longing, or whatever that wants to be taken care of, or sometimes it is just your body reacting to being overloaded, or chaos, or a lack of sleep, or just confused. Just because you had a picture that scared you, doesn’t mean it is true. Just because you had a bad feeling, doesn’t mean it is a lesson you need to learn. Just because you had a download, and the lighting was really nice, doesn’t mean you should believe it.

old: Before trying to interpret the state, ask a simpler question:
new: What is a simpler question to ask yourself, before you even try to interpret it?

old: Read this slowly into a recorder, speak it aloud, or learn its movement and use silent words if that comes easily. Choose one anchor—a sound, bodily contact, or your two-hand practice—and an opening phrase. Keep using the same anchor where the words refer to it. Pause between paragraphs; don’t read the delivery directions aloud.
new: Practise reading this slowly, perhaps into a recorder, or just reading aloud, or better still, learn it and say the words silently. You might choose to use one of the three anchors, sound, bodily contact or two hands etc, and use that throughout, also choose an opening phrase. Whenever it says, say for example, ‘the anchor’, use the one you’ve chosen. Pause for a few moments at the end of each paragraph. Don’t read aloud the instructions for how you are going to read this.

old: Let your eyes settle somewhere in the room, somewhere they can rest for a little while, and notice the difference between looking for something and letting what is already there come into view.
new: Allow your eyes to settle on something in the room….

old: There is a surface beneath you. Notice where you meet it … the contact, the pressure, whatever you can actually feel. And while you notice that, a sound may reach you, or a breath may draw your attention, without needing you to arrange either one.
new: As you notice the surface, notice the feel of the contact…notice a sound…notice your breath…..

old: You can give this a little time.
new: There’s time to do this.

old: A thought about the day may still be here. A thought about whether you’re doing this properly may be here too. There is room to notice a thought and return to the anchor you chose, without finishing the thought first.
new: It could be a thought about something that’s happened in the day, or it could be a thought about doing this. Whatever it is, can you, even with that thought there, turn your attention to the anchor….

old: And as you return, you may find one detail that holds your interest … something about the sound, or the contact, or that particular way of listening … and let attention stay with it long enough to become curious.
new: You might find something that holds your interest, perhaps something in the sound, contact, or your listening.

old: Perhaps you can give yourself the time you would give someone you care about who has begun to speak and hasn’t yet found the words. You can remain nearby, listening, without finishing their sentence for them.
new: You might give this time to yourself as you might to someone dear to you who is talking to you. Perhaps the words are not yet fully formed yet, but you are there, listening.

old: Let your chosen phrase come to mind now. Say it as an invitation, and notice how it is received.
new: Let yourself be invited to think of your chosen phrase and notice how you receive this.

old: As you continue, your eyes can close, soften, or stay open. Let that be a choice you make. Listening may deepen while a sound from the room remains available in the background.
new: You might close, soften or open your eyes as you proceed. Perhaps you might let your listening deepen, allowing the sound of what is going on around you to remain in the background.

old: Count slowly from five to one. Give each number its own moment.
new: Counting slowly from 5 to 1.

old: Five. Notice your chosen anchor again. Four. Let attention gather around what you find. Three. Leave a little space after the words. Two. Listen into that space, without preparing an answer. One. Stay here for a moment.
new: 5, perhaps notice again your chosen anchor for today, 4, notice, 3, space, 2, listen, 1, stay

old: Bring your chosen concern lightly to mind, or remain with your wish for contact. Let it be present without rehearsing its whole story.
new: Bring to mind your chosen concern or just the wish to contact.

old: What am I noticing now?
new: Notice what you notice.

old: Give the response time to take its own form. It might be a sensation, a few words, an image, a feeling, or an impulse to move. There may be nothing clear yet.
new: Allow yourself some time to notice what is coming for you, sensations, words, images, feelings, movements or even nothing for now.

old: Leave room to notice, with words or without them.
new: Allow yourself some time to notice what you notice, with or without words.

old: Reverse whatever you used to enter. If you floated, regain chosen weight. If you became small, return to ordinary scale. If you met a younger state or several parts, confirm present wholeness, body ownership, and adult judgment. If you traveled, come back by the same route. Keep only the qualities you deliberately chose.
new: Bring yourself out of the session in reverse order to how you got into it. If you floated up, then float back down. Make sure you’re coming back down in the weight you want to be. If you shrank yourself, make sure you’re growing back to your normal size. If you went back to a younger version of yourself, or met other parts of yourself, make sure you know that you’re whole now, in this body, using the judgement of the age you are now. If you traveled somewhere, come back the same way you left, but make sure you’re not bringing anything back with you that you didn’t mean to.

old: “I bring back only what is useful now. The rest can remain safely held until there is more capacity. I return to the room, the body, the day, and one honest action. All instructions to deepen or remain in this session are finished. I keep only the ordinary-life intention or future-practice cue I consciously chose; neither keeps today’s altered state running. I am myself, in my body, with adult judgment fully available.”
new: “Bring back with you only that which will be of use to you in your life now. Store away that which is not, until such time as you wish to use it. Come back now to this place, back into your body, back into normal life, back into the one honest action. There are no more instructions to keep you in this altered state, there is no instruction to take with you into normal life that will keep you in this altered state, there is no instruction to use in the future that will put you into this altered state again.

old: One — feel the body’s contact and chosen weight. Two — let the breath return to its ordinary rhythm. Three — hear the room and name where you are. Four — move fingers, toes, shoulders, and eyes. Five — eyes open, present, ordinary, clear. The session has ended.
new: Count yourself out of the session now. 1. Coming back now into your body, back into the weight you chose to have. 2. Coming back into your normal breathing pattern. 3. Hearing the sound in the room around you now, knowing where you are. 4. Moving your fingers and your toes, your shoulders and your eyes. 5. Opening your eyes, feeling normal, feeling present, the session is now over.”

old: Name the day or date. Look left, right, near, and far. Move before standing, and stand only when steady. Check that you are actually oriented and alert; repeating the count is not proof of a complete return. Note only what actually appeared, and any action it calls for. Then do something normal.
new: Bring yourself out by opening your eyes and saying to yourself where you are, and what day or date it is. Look to the left, look to the right, look at something near, look at something far away. Move around a bit, then stand up when you feel you can do so without falling over. Make sure that you are oriented and alert. Don’t just count, and think that because you were told to, that you are alert and oriented. Note to yourself what if anything came up in the session, and what if anything you need to do about it, and go and do something normal.

old: If a recording stops unexpectedly: say, “The recording stopped and the session is over.” Open your eyes, name the location and day, press your feet or hands into a surface, move, look around, and use the five-step count. Don’t wait for the missing narrator to release you.
new: In the event that the recording stops before it should, say to yourself, “the recording has stopped, the session is over”, and use the above method to come out. Open your eyes, say where you are, say what day it is, push down with your feet or hands, move about, look around, and if need be use the 5 step method.

old: Sleep is separate. A sleep recording may end in sleep or quiet rest. A waking recording shouldn’t end by preserving a role, reduced judgment, impaired movement, blankness, an undefined reset word, or an invitation to remain altered indefinitely.
new: Note: When using a recording to take you to sleep, it is allright for the recording to put you to sleep, or leave you in a quiet resting state. However a recording used when awake, should not leave you in a role, with lowered judgement, impaired movement capabilities, blank, with an undefined reset word, invited to remain in an altered state, etc.
